title: Microsoft 365 ↔ Google Workspace Coexistence (Mail Routing, Free/Busy, Directory Sync)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Make Microsoft and Google work as one during the transition
problem: For months during a 150k-user migration, Microsoft and Google run side by side — and users expect mail, calendars, and directory to just work across both. This solution designs and implements M365 ↔ Google Workspace coexistence: split/shared mail routing, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync, so the two ecosystems behave as one until consolidation, executed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the coexistence model (mail routing/split delivery, free/busy interop, directory sync) and how it bridges the transition.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (both tenants + admin access, DNS/mail-flow control, directory-sync mechanism, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.
Implementation Guide — exact steps to configure mail routing/split delivery, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync, validate interop on a pilot, then expand.
5 supporting scripts — coexistence-readiness discovery, per-user interop validation (mail/free-busy/directory), a coexistence coverage report, safe remediation, and a scope helper.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (mail routes, free/busy resolves, directory in sync) plus Best Practices for a stable transition period.
short: Design and run M365 ↔ Google Workspace coexistence — mail routing/split delivery, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync — so both ecosystems behave as one during the transition, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
